identity.title: A Computational Framework for Modeling Emergence of Color Vision in the Human Brain

problem.claim: Explain how the brain infers color vision and its dimensionality from optic-nerve signals despite unknown eye encoding properties.

gap.claim: Existing work often assumes color dimensionality is known in advance and overlooks cortical development and internal color-space representation.

contributions.claim: A computational framework jointly simulating the eye and cortex to model the emergence of human color vision.
A biologically grounded eye simulation engine producing optic-nerve signals from natural images, paired with cortical self-supervised prediction under natural eye motions.
A model in which color dimensionality emerges from disentangling retinal invariants from sensory signals.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe their work as the first simulation that boosts color dimensionality in a way observed in squirrel-monkey gene therapy, and as demonstrating the possibility of increasing human color vision from 3D to 4D.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the cortical model naturally learns color vision by disentangling retinal invariants from sensory signals.
The authors report that simulations with N color-photoreceptor types yield N-dimensional color vision, with the result verified through formal colorimetry.
The authors report a simulation reproducing boosted color dimensionality observed in squirrel-monkey gene therapy and indicating possible enhancement of human color vision from 3D to 4D.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper frames color decoding from optic-nerve signals as an inferential mystery involving unknown retinal encoding and color dimensionality.
It identifies a priori dimensionality assumptions in existing research and introduces a joint eye–cortex computational framework.
The authors build an eye simulation driven by natural images and propose cortical self-supervised learning from signal fluctuations during eye motion.
They report emergent color vision, N-to-N dimensionality matching under formal colorimetry, and simulated dimensionality enhancement from 3D to 4D.

source_observation.claim: The abstract aligns each modeling component with a specific biological signal source or learning condition: eye simulation generates optic-nerve inputs, while cortical learning predicts fluctuations under natural eye motions.

lessons.interpretation: This component-to-mechanism alignment makes the proposed explanation easier to evaluate conceptually.
lessons.application: When presenting a biologically motivated model, explicitly map each module to its biological input, constraint, and learning signal.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when the work is intentionally abstract and does not claim biological plausibility.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify simulation parameters, datasets or natural-image coverage, training details, baselines, quantitative colorimetry results, or statistical analyses.
The reported 3D-to-4D enhancement is described as a possibility; the abstract does not establish performance in humans or clinical feasibility.
The abstract does not provide details of the formal colorimetry protocol or how closely the simulation matches gene-therapy observations.
